objectNotes.doActions: 66 DoActions total, all registered by ONE function on Linux: the jag::MiniMenu ctor FUN_00078b4e installs every sender inline (there is no second component-action registrar as there is on Windows). Action object layout: +0x00 client ctx, +0x10 invoker thunk, +0x18 sender fn (all three written at runtime by the ctor), +0x20 dispatch id, +0x24 kind (both written by the static initializer FUN_000af050). Layout re-derived from this binary and validated by reproducing five already-correct rows exactly before any change: SELECT_NPC 8, WALK 23, DIALOGUE 30, SELECT_TILE 59, and COMPONENT 57 / COMPONENT_SIXPLUS 1007 sharing one sender. LOC FAMILY CORRECTED 2026-07: the loc rows were mis-paired, every name sitting one slot below its true sender, which left OBJECT_4 with no address at all (0x0, so DoActionOpcode.OBJECT_4.fire() was a no-op). True kind-3 mapping is id 1 SELECT_OBJECT 0x162af0, 2 OBJECT_1 0x162bc0, 3 OBJECT_2 0x162ba0, 4 OBJECT_3 0x162b80, 5 OBJECT_4 0x162b60, 1001 OBJECT_5 0x162b40, 1002 OBJECT_6 0x162b20. SELECT_OBJECT's sender was previously absent from the table entirely; it is the only loc sender that branches on jag::g_protocolRevision (descriptor DAT_016844b0 = ClientProt op 9 size 17 below 0x3b5, else DAT_01683e10 = op 116 size 18) and the only one SendOpLoc special-cases to also emit the pending selection state, and FUN_001cdfa0 groups its action object with the other select-family objects (SELECT_TILE, SELECT_NPC, SELECT_GROUND_ITEM, PLAYER_SELECT, COMP_ON_PLAYER, SELECT_COMPONENT_ITEM) and no other loc action. Each of DoOpLoc1..6 dispatches a distinct fixed-size-9 ClientProt op (41, 70, 33, 91, 1, 88), so a wrong pairing would have sent the wrong in-game action rather than failing loudly. ALIAS IDS: Linux has the same alias-copy pattern as Windows - the ctor calls FUN_00cbee00(dst,src) to copy a registered object's callable into a second object under another id, giving loc 1001/1002 also as 6/7 (recorded as OBJECT_5_ALT/OBJECT_6_ALT), npc 2009-2013/3003 also as 9-13/1003, player 44-53 also as 2044-2053. Which id of a pair the client actually dispatches at runtime is UNKNOWN and matters only for DoActionOpcode.getActionById; no existing row's id was flipped between members of a pair. Next lead for that: capture real menu clicks on a 5-op and a 6-op loc and read the dispatched id. The third-party 951-4 table agrees on all 47 DoOp addresses it lists.

objectNotes.OHeightMap: jag::game::HeightMap (World[HEIGHT_MAP]). GetFineHeight: grid = *(HeightMap + GRID); the grid's region bounds & map-square vector ARE the OWorld build-area fields (MAPSQUARE_*_OFFSET/_MAX, MAPSQUARES_VECTOR), so those are referenced from OWorld, not duplicated. Each vector cell (CELL_STRIDE) holds the per-map- square ORegionHeightContainer at +CELL_CONTAINER; an empty cell reads BASE + EMPTY_CELL_SENTINEL_REL.
objectNotes.ORegionHeightContainer: jag::game::RegionHeightContainer — per-map-square height data. SampleRegionFineHeight@0x0049aff0 selects PRIMARY or FALLBACK (usable iff byte[READY_LO]==byte[READY_HI]; byte[NOT_LOADED_FLAG]!=0 => not loaded), samples the per-plane int32 vertex grid (PLANE_VEC_*, or PLANE0_BRIDGE_GRID for plane 0), then ADDS the signed-int16 LINK_HEIGHT grid (SampleTileLinkHeightOffset@0x0047ab50 — raised platforms/bridge decks).
objectNotes.OMapSquare: +0x18 was inserted before LOCATION_CONTAINERS (LocationContainerAt reads [MS+0xeb80] in 949-1 vs [MS+0xeb68] in 948-5). Header stable: CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG@0x70 and the height-container ptr@0x90 are read at the same offsets in both builds, so everything <=0xb0 is unshifted. 950-1: the chunk-size conditional was DELETED from the client. GetLocationContainerAt no longer tests COMPOSITE_DATA at all - the divisor is a hard-coded 16 on both axes (signed-shift idiom), so CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG has no reader left and its value here is only the still-live COMPOSITE_DATA displacement. Two further changes in the same accessor: the inner element stride is now 0x10 (was 8), and each element is a shared_ptr pair whose container pointer lives at element+8 (was a bare pointer at element+0) - callers load [result+8]. Confirmed identically on Linux and Windows. ENGINE ACTION REQUIRED in SceneManager.kt: chunkSize must stop branching on the flag, the inner Vector element size must go 0x8 -> LOCATION_CONTAINER_ENTRY_STRIDE, and the container deref must go through LOCATION_CONTAINER_ENTRY_PTR_OFFSET. Updating the stride alone leaves the pointer read silently wrong.

objectNotes.ONPC: CURRENT_HP/MAX_HP hold a 0-100 health RATIO, not absolute hitpoints — the NXT client is only told the headbar proportion. Verified live on 949-1: Man, Cow, Skoblin and Guard all read 100/100 at full health, with every neighbouring dword zero, so the values are deliberate rather than garbage. A displacement scan of .text finds no direct dword access at either offset; the write goes through the update-mask handler's computed pointer. Do not 'correct' these to absolute HP on that scan alone — still unconfirmed is whether they track damage, which needs an NPC observed at partial health.
objectNotes.OInterfaceComponent: 950-1: the struct was REORGANIZED, not shifted - measured deltas across directly-read field pairs are non-monotonic, so no field may be predicted from another. ITEM_ID/STACK_SIZE and MODEL_ID/MODEL_OBJECT belong to DIFFERENT component subclasses and now overlap: reading a model field off an obj-class component returns the obj field's bytes. Discriminate on the component's vtable type call before reading any of the four. COMPONENT_TYPE remains a deliberate negative - the CS2 type tag is consumed by the component factory to pick the C++ subclass and is never written back onto the object.
